_about: Misconceptions that error items target. home is the lesson whose concept it belongs to; an item in that lesson or a later one is on the path (a later one is a spiral). See AUTHORING.md, Error tasks.

algebra-juxtaposition.text: 2x with x = 4 is read as 24 (the digits side by side) instead of 2 × 4 = 8.

angle-from-sides.text: The turn is guessed or multiplied instead of worked out as 360 / sides.

assign-vs-compare.text: A single = is used to ask whether two things are equal.

list-index-range.text: A list of n items has a place n; places run from 0 to n - 1.

name-rebinding.text: Defining (or importing) a name twice keeps both; in fact the later one silently replaces the earlier.

copied-code.text: Copying working code is free; in fact every copy must be fixed separately.

return-vs-print.text: print gives a value back; only return does, and a function without return gives None.

handler-call-vs-pass.text: Handing over a handler with brackets calls it at once instead of passing the function.

and-vs-or.text: Conditions that must all hold are joined with or instead of and.

html-error-message.text: A mistake in HTML stops the page with an error message, as in Python; the browser actually shows its best guess and says nothing.

tag-overlap.text: Tags can close in any order, so they overlap (…) instead of nesting.

list-item-outside.text: An <li> works anywhere, not only inside a <ul> or <ol>.

table-row-cells.text: A row can have fewer cells than the others, and the browser lines the table up anyway.

selector-mismatch.text: A rule styles an element even when its selector does not exactly match the tag or class (a typo, or a class without its dot).

css-missing-unit.text: A size works without a unit, as in padding: 10.

flex-on-items.text: display: flex goes on the items to line them up, instead of on the box that holds them.

label-not-linked.text: A label belongs to the input next to it, whatever its for says.

img-file-name.text: The browser finds a picture from a name close to the real file name; the name, extension and capitals must match exactly.

semantic-tags-look.text: Section tags such as header and footer change how a page looks or where things go; they only name the parts, and CSS decides the look.

grid-on-items.text: display: grid and its columns go on each item, instead of on the box that holds them.
